# Rev2D

Studio scenes: read docs/SCENE.md (`rev2d docs scene`). Compose library assets, camera, narration
cues, pose changes and animated UI; scene validate → sheet/frame → analyze → render. MCP exposes
rev2d_scene_validate, rev2d_scene_frame, rev2d_scene_sheet, rev2d_scene_analyze and rev2d_scene_render.
PNG sequences need no ffmpeg; MP4/GIF stream through optional external ffmpeg without a shell.

> Rev2D is an AI-friendly 2D rigging and animation toolkit in the spirit of Live2D Cubism and Spine, written in TypeScript. A model is one JSON file (`*.r2d.json`) with parameters, bones, warp deformers, parts (vector shapes, images, meshes), keyform bindings, IK (with softness and stretch), pendulum physics and layered animations, all in canvas-pixel coordinates (+y down, clockwise degrees). The `rev2d` CLI and an MCP server validate models with precise diagnostics, render them deterministically without a GPU (with debug overlays, parameter-sweep, overview and animation contact sheets, GIFs), report exact pose numbers (IK reach, physics outputs, mapped points, tables over time), analyze whole animations (physics clamping, IK snap risk, loop seams), and apply atomic, validated edit operations; `rev2d edit [model | dir]` opens a live-reloading web editor (React + WebGL2) that the AI can observe and drive, with file management confined to a workspace root (File menu: new from a template, open, save as, import, download, close; a start screen with example cards). `rev2d import spine|live2d` and `rev2d export spine|live2d` (MCP `rev2d_import`, `rev2d_export`; editor File menu) convert Spine skeleton exports and Live2D motion / expression / physics / display-info JSON in and out, with a report of everything approximated or dropped; the Live2D .moc3 model binary is not supported. `rev2d avatar new|grid|overlay|validate|build|poses|variants` turns ONE illustration (ideally a front-facing bust on a transparent background) into an ordinary animated model: landmarks placed in `avatar.json` (by an agent reading coordinate grids, or by a person dragging handles in the editor's Avatar mode) cut the picture into layers, and the build generates head turn and tilt, blinking and gaze, a talking mouth, brows, blush, breathing, body sway, hair and accessory physics, six animations and review sheets; drawn closed eyes and mouth shapes from an image generator (with consent) replace the mesh deformation, and `src/lipsync` turns kana / Hangul / romaji text or WAV loudness into MouthOpen / MouthForm motion. The editor (iOS-inspired design, light / dark, English / Korean / Japanese) can also run the Codex CLI or Claude Code in its AI panel with the person's own login (loopback only, token-protected).

Start with AGENTS.md (for avatars: `rev2d docs avatar`, docs/AVATAR.md): it explains the mental model, the validate → render → sheet → inspect → analyze → ops verification loop, how to read diagnostics and notes, the property address grammar, the standard parameter signs (AngleX > 0 turns toward the screen right, AngleY > 0 looks up, L = the character's left = screen right) and common mistakes. Run tools with `node bin/rev2d.js <command>` (or `npx rev2d` inside the repository); MCP: `node bin/rev2d.js mcp` over stdio, then call `rev2d_guide`. Explicit parameter values beat animations and physics; physics steps at 60 Hz from rest (a single pose simulates at most the 60 s before its time). With the editor open, `rev2d editor state|screenshot` shows what the human sees and `rev2d editor command --open <file>` (MCP `rev2d_editor_command {type: "open"}`) switches it to another model of its workspace; `--model <file>` finds the editor that has the file open, else the one whose workspace root contains it.

## Docs

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): guide for AI agents: mental model, parameter conventions, verification loop (render notes, sheets, inspect, analyze), diagnostics, address cheat sheet, ops cheat sheet, common mistakes, MCP tools, working with a human in the live editor (workspace root, opening files for them, finding the right editor, Avatar mode, the in-app AI panel), Spine and Live2D files, avatars from one illustration (the 8-step loop and the evidence checklist); developing Rev2D (commands, module boundaries incl. src/avatar, src/lipsync, src/node/agent and the editor's shell / design / i18n / ai / avatar folders, conventions, where to add features)
- [docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md): authoritative model format and evaluation semantics (coordinates, parameter naming and signs, objects, addresses, bindings, animations with smooth ease, track offset and layers, IK with softness/stretch and diagnostics, physics, per-frame pipeline, Pose and mapPoint)
- [docs/RECIPES.md](docs/RECIPES.md): copy-paste op batches, each with the commands that verify it (all executed by the test suite): head turn, blink, mouth morphs, breathing, hair physics, arm IK, skinning, squash & stretch, draw order, blend modes, textures, layered animations, events, clean closed eyes, gestures over an idle (add, once, compose), a hat on a turning head (follow), markings under an outline, pixel parameter rigs, a walk cycle, physics tuning with analyze, recolor
- [docs/OPS.md](docs/OPS.md): edit operations (add and update with bone world position / worldRotation, remove, rename, set, bind with relative values, bind_linear, bind_warp, follow, unbind, key, unkey, move, recolor, compose, patch), reference handling and the bind_warp head-turn math
- [docs/CLI.md](docs/CLI.md): every rev2d command, flag, exit code, note and --json output shape (including animation layer syntax, sampling flags, inspect series/tracks and analyze)
- [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md): MCP server setup (Claude Code and other clients), the 18 tools (`rev2d_docs` topics include `avatar`), conventions, editor bridge, troubleshooting
- [docs/INTEROP.md](docs/INTEROP.md): Spine and Live2D interop: Spine 3.8-4.2 skeleton JSON + atlas import (a new model; shear, inheritance modes, transform constraints and image sequences emulated, path / physics constraints and two-color tint reported) and export (Spine 4.x JSON + atlas + PNG pages, everything baked); Live2D motion3 / exp3 / physics3 / cdi3 / model3 JSON import (as ops into a model) and export; the .moc3 binary is not supported (motions, physics and names move by parameter id); support matrix, coordinate conversion, the standard parameter map, reports with stable codes, workflows (AI-made Live2D motions, bringing a Spine character in, sending a rig to Spine runtimes), limitations
- [docs/AVATAR.md](docs/AVATAR.md): an animated avatar from one illustration, the working guide (`rev2d docs avatar`): what it can and cannot do, the project folder, the workflow (vision check, coordinate grids, placing every landmark group, validate, overlay, build, review sheets, fix loop, `post` ops), the generated parameters, parts, physics and animations, drawn variants (request, masks, the import check, consent, stale sprites), lip sync from text or WAV, the editor's Avatar mode and AI tasks, Mesh Avatar Studio import, common `avatar-*` diagnostics with fixes
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): pipeline, module responsibilities, data contracts, determinism guarantees, editor protocol (server modules, endpoints incl. workspace file management, avatar mode and the agent bridge, SSE events, workspace-root path safety), the editor UI (shell, workspace modes and mode documents, panels, design system, languages, Avatar mode, AI panel), the avatar builder and lip sync, extension points
- [docs/AGENT-BRIDGE.md](docs/AGENT-BRIDGE.md): coding agents inside the editor (Codex CLI, Claude Code): the AI panel, protocol (`/api/session`, `/api/agent/*`, SSE `agent-job`), security model (loopback only, per-server token, no shell, two sandboxes), providers, the preamble and task templates (`avatar-create`, `avatar-variants`), logs, troubleshooting (the Windows Codex sandbox setting)
- [docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md): the editor's iOS / iPadOS-inspired design language: research, principles, tokens (appearance, colour, materials, shape, type), components, the editor layout, accessibility, assets and legal limits

## Examples

- [examples/README.md](examples/README.md): the five example models and a feature matrix of the techniques each one uses
- [examples/minimal/minimal.r2d.json](examples/minimal/minimal.r2d.json): the smallest complete rig (one parameter, bone, warp, binding and animation)
- [examples/hana/hana.r2d.json](examples/hana/hana.r2d.json): Live2D-style bust: 3x3 head-turn warp grid, path-morph eyes and mouth, masks, hair physics
- [examples/robot-arm/robot-arm.r2d.json](examples/robot-arm/robot-arm.r2d.json): Spine-style skeleton: two-bone IK, skinning, cable physics
- [examples/slime/slime.r2d.json](examples/slime/slime.r2d.json): squash and stretch, blend modes, events
- [examples/textured/textured.r2d.json](examples/textured/textured.r2d.json): PNG textures, atlas crops in warps, textured mesh

## Media

- [docs/media/rev2d-demo.mp4](docs/media/rev2d-demo.mp4): 65 s demo video (1280x720, real footage; English headlines, Korean captions): the example rigs animating, one JSON file per model, the AI verification loop (overlays, sweep sheets, analyze), an AI editing a model live while the web editor reacts, the editor's File menu and start screen, the MCP tools
- [docs/media/clip-ai-live-edit.mp4](docs/media/clip-ai-live-edit.mp4), [docs/media/clip-verify.mp4](docs/media/clip-verify.mp4), [docs/media/clip-showcase.mp4](docs/media/clip-showcase.mp4): short clips of those scenes; [docs/media/hero.gif](docs/media/hero.gif) and [docs/media/ai-live-edit.gif](docs/media/ai-live-edit.gif) as GIFs

## Optional

- [README.md](README.md): project overview, how AI agents use Rev2D (verify loop, MCP setup, live editor bridge, example prompts), avatar from one illustration, the editor and its AI panel, feature map against Live2D/Spine concepts, quick start; [README.ko.md](README.ko.md) is the Korean edition
- [src/core/schema.ts](src/core/schema.ts): the zod schema that defines the format (`rev2d schema` prints it as JSON Schema)
- [src/mcp/guide.ts](src/mcp/guide.ts): the compact quickstart served by the `rev2d_guide` MCP tool
- [src/avatar/DESIGN.md](src/avatar/DESIGN.md): how the avatar builder works inside (pipeline, the structure of the generated model, deformation fields, drawn variants, quality bar)
- [src/avatar/schema.ts](src/avatar/schema.ts): the zod schema of `avatar.json` (`rev2d avatar schema` prints it as JSON Schema)

- [Reusable asset libraries](docs/LIBRARY.md): catalogue, uniform-background keying, generation requests, avatar build provenance, contact sheets and MCP tools.
